answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because saffron only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, juniper is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any mirror approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
